hook.line: When one thing leads to another, spoken Spanish says *por eso*. In an essay or a formal email you need something with more weight, and the choice of connector decides the mood of the verb that follows.
hook.es: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazara.
hook.en: There was no agreement; hence the meeting was postponed.

examples.es: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazara.
examples.en: There was no agreement; hence the meeting was postponed.

examples.es: Así pues, la decisión es nuestra.
Llegó tarde, de manera que perdió el vuelo.
examples.en: He arrived late, so he missed the flight.

examples.es: Por consiguiente, se suspende la obra.
Hubo mucho ruido; de ahí que no se oyera la pregunta.
examples.en: There was a lot of noise; hence the question could not be heard.

examples.es: No tengo la contraseña; de ahí que no pueda entrar.
examples.en: I don't have the password; hence I can't get in.

examples.es: Salió temprano, de manera que llegó a tiempo.
examples.en: She left early, so she arrived on time.

rule:
Spanish has four formal ways to say "so" or "hence":
*Así pues* and *por consiguiente* start a sentence and are followed by a normal verb: *así pues, la decisión es nuestra*.
*De manera que* also takes a normal verb when you simply report what happened: *llegó tarde, de manera que perdió el vuelo*.
*De ahí que* is the one to watch. It always takes the subjunctive, because you are not announcing the result as news, you are presenting it as the known consequence: *de ahí que la reunión se aplazara*, *de ahí que no pueda entrar*.

If the main sentence is in the past, the verb after *de ahí que* is the past subjunctive (*se aplazara*, *oyera*). If it is in the present, it is the present subjunctive (*pueda*).
smallPrint: Teachers call these consecutive connectors, because they introduce a consequence. *De ahí que* is the only one here that forces the subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazara.
options: There was no agreement; hence the meeting was postponed.
There was no agreement; hence the meeting will be postponed.
There was agreement; hence the meeting was postponed.

readAndPick.es: Llegó tarde, de manera que perdió el vuelo.
options: He arrived late, so he missed the flight.
He arrives late, so he misses the flight.
He arrived late, so he will miss the flight.

readAndPick.es: No tengo la contraseña; de ahí que no pueda entrar.
options: I don't have the password; hence I could not get in.
I don't have the password; hence I can't get in.
I had the password; hence I can't get in.

readAndPick.es: Así pues, la decisión es nuestra.
options: Thus, the decision is ours.
Thus, the decision was theirs.
Thus, the decision will be ours.

readAndPick.es: Hubo mucho ruido; de ahí que no se oyera la pregunta.
options: There was a lot of noise; hence the question is not heard.
There was a lot of noise; hence the question could not be heard.
There will be a lot of noise; hence the question could not be heard.

readAndPick.es: Por consiguiente, se suspende la obra.
options: Consequently, the works were suspended.
Consequently, the works are suspended.
Consequently, the works were not suspended.

readAndPick.es: Salió temprano, de manera que llegó a tiempo.
options: She left early, so she arrives on time.
She left early, so she arrived late.
She left early, so she arrived on time.

readAndPick.es: El plazo terminó; de ahí que el trámite se cancelara.
options: The deadline ended; hence the procedure was cancelled.
The deadline ends; hence the procedure is cancelled.
The deadline ended; hence the procedure will be cancelled.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Hubo mucho ruido; de ahí que no se ___ la pregunta.* (*oyó* or *oyera*) There was a lot of noise; hence the question could not be heard.
yourTurn.answer: Hubo mucho ruido; de ahí que no se oyera la pregunta.
yourTurn.why: *De ahí que* takes the subjunctive, and the past needs *oyera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Salió temprano, de manera que ___ a tiempo.* (*llegó* or *llegara*) She left early, so she arrived on time.
yourTurn.answer: Salió temprano, de manera que llegó a tiempo.
yourTurn.why: Here you report a fact, so *de manera que* takes the normal past, *llegó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Consequently, the works are suspended.
yourTurn.answer: Por consiguiente, se suspende la obra.
yourTurn.why: *Por consiguiente* starts the sentence and takes a normal verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't have the password; hence I can't get in.
yourTurn.answer: No tengo la contraseña; de ahí que no pueda entrar.
yourTurn.why: The main verb is in the present, so *de ahí que* needs the present subjunctive *pueda*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: He arrived late, so he missed the flight.
yourTurn.answer: Llegó tarde, de manera que perdió el vuelo.
yourTurn.why: A plain result after *de manera que* uses the normal past.

yourTurn.prompt: Join with *de ahí que*, in the past: *La obra no tenía permiso. El barrio protestó.*
yourTurn.answer: La obra no tenía permiso; de ahí que el barrio protestara.
accept: La obra no tenía permiso, de ahí que el barrio protestara.
yourTurn.why: Past main verb, so the past subjunctive *protestara* follows *de ahí que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Start with *así pues*: *La decisión es nuestra.*
yourTurn.answer: Así pues, la decisión es nuestra.
yourTurn.why: *Así pues* sits at the front and the verb stays normal.

pitfalls.wrong: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazó.
pitfalls.right: No hubo acuerdo; de ahí que la reunión se aplazara.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *De ahí que* always needs the subjunctive, even for something that really happened.

pitfalls.wrong: No tengo la contraseña; de ahí que no puedo entrar.
pitfalls.right: No tengo la contraseña; de ahí que no pueda entrar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *de ahí que* the present needs *pueda*, not *puedo*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hubo mucho ruido; de ahí no se oyera la pregunta.
pitfalls.right: Hubo mucho ruido; de ahí que no se oyera la pregunta.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The *que* is part of the connector: *de ahí que*.

personal: Think of something that happened to you this week and what followed from it. Say it with *de ahí que* or *de manera que*.
